_comment: Reviewer-facing catalog: WHAT each cloud-sandbox scenario is and HOW it is validated. Folded into the review HTML by gen-review-report.py alongside the live KR frames. Keep ids in sync with kr-review-run.sh.

invariant.title: Global no-error invariant (applies to every scenario)
invariant.what: At the end of EVERY scenario, no error text may be visible anywhere on screen — 'Internal error', 'rejected by sandbox', 'Remote session source', raw session-uuid 'not found', 'Failed to …', 'error occurred' — with exactly two deliberate exceptions: the humanized gate refusals ('… is not available for a cloud session yet.') and the provider-gate screen ('Source provider not found' + setup handoff).
invariant.how: kr-review-run.sh no_error_check(): dumps the live screen, greps for the error signatures, subtracts the two allowlisted shapes; any surviving row fails the scenario and is recorded verbatim in the manifest (shown as 'error row:' notes below the checks). This replaces per-command error tests by design decision — raw wire errors are a bug in ANY flow, not just /knowledge or /plan.

S01.covers: Basic user story 1 (start a cloud session); bug #30 (startup tools labelled Cancelled) — CLI side
S01.what: A user runs `kiro chat --cloud`. They should see the connect checklist progress (kiro.dev, GitHub, session created, repo count), end at a usable prompt, and the persistent ☁ Cloud footer chip — with no phantom 'Cancelled' tool rows from sandbox startup prefetches.
S01.how: Boot the real TUI + published KAS against the mock BFF with --cloud. Poll the live screen for each checklist milestone in order ('Cloud session created', 'repositories found', 'ask a question'), then assert the Cloud footer chip is present and 'Cancelled' appears nowhere. Frame captured at the settled state. Mirrors E2E cloud-sessions.test.ts t1.
S01.limits: The mock serves no startup tool frames, so the Cancelled check pins only client-synthesized rows; the real prefetch path (bug #30's actual trigger) needs a prod-mode run.

S02.what: A user without a GitHub/GitLab connection starts a cloud session. Instead of a broken chat, they get a gate screen explaining the requirement and a Kiro Web handoff to complete the connection — and no chat prompt while gated.
S02.how: Restart the mock BFF with MOCK_BFF_NO_PROVIDER=1 (ListAvailableProviders returns DISCONNECTED; CheckProviderSetup returns the setup URL). Boot --cloud, wait for the gate text, assert the kiro.dev/browser handoff is offered and 'ask a question' is absent. The provider-gate screen is one of the two allowlisted 'deliberate block' shapes in the no-error invariant. Mirrors E2E t2.

S03.covers: Basic user story 3 (repo selection); bug #28 (Tab to switch panels / interactive Selected section); pink-checkmark nit — both fixed by #3656
S03.what: The /repo picker lists the provider's repos with a two-panel layout. Space toggles selection; Tab moves focus to the Selected panel where space UNCHECKS (pre-fix the Selected panel was inert); the checked row shows its ✓ mark.
S03.how: Type /repo, wait for the mock's 3 repos to render, assert the 'tab to switch panels' hint. Press space and pin the header counter 'Selected(1)' (unambiguous — titles can't fake it). Press Tab then space and pin 'Selected(0)'. Frames at open/selected/unchecked. Mirrors E2E cloud-repo-picker.test.ts (which additionally regex-pins the [✓] mark placement).

S04.covers: Basic user story 3b (--repo flag); known-behavior note 'repo is not cloned until the first message'
S04.what: `--cloud --repo kiro-team/banana-service` binds the repo directly: footer shows it, the interactive picker never opens, and nothing clones before the first message (same deferred-clone behavior as Kiro Web).
S04.how: Boot with the flag; assert the repo name renders, 'space to toggle' (picker) is absent, and 'cloning' is absent. The clone-deferred check is gated behind the footer-bind positive so it can't pass vacuously when the session never booted. Mirrors E2E t4.

S05.covers: Bugs #19 (/chat save local-path error), #8/#22 (/context errors), and the '!bash runs locally' launch blocker — gates from #3651/#3656
S05.what: Commands that cannot work in a cloud session yet must refuse with the humanized gate message — never a raw error, never a local-machine side effect. /chat save|load and /context add are gated; `!` shell escape must refuse AND never execute the command locally.
S05.how: Type each command; wait for '… is not available for a cloud session yet.'. For /chat save additionally assert the old failure shape (leaked ~/.kiro/sessions path) is absent. For the shell escape, count occurrences of a marker string: every occurrence must belong to the echoed input row ('!echo LEAKED_LOCAL_EXEC'); a bare-marker row would be the command's stdout = local execution leak. Ends with the global no-error check. Mirrors E2E cloud-command-gates.test.ts t1-t3.
S05.limits: Per design decision there is NO dedicated /knowledge//plan error test — those commands are covered by the global no-error invariant like every other flow.

S06.covers: Bugs #2 (completed tools replay as interrupted), #29 (resume stopped replaying), #32 (first prompt re-replays history); story 5 (attach with full trajectory); resume wording UX (#3656); fixes #3664
S06.what: Resuming a cloud session replays the FULL prior trajectory — user rows, agent rows, and tool calls rendered with their true completed status (not 'Cancelled'/'interrupted') — under the 'Resuming…/✓ Cloud session resumed' checklist wording. Submitting a new prompt afterwards must not re-render the history a second time.
S06.how: Mock BFF serves a canned two-turn transcript for the banana session as a REAL AWS event stream (lean-dialect frames, per-turn end_turn done frames, session_loaded sentinel) — the exact wire shape a suspended-sandbox resume serves in production, so KAS's reconstruction fold runs for real. Boot with --resume-id <banana>, wait for both turns' text and the Shell tool row, assert no Cancelled/interrupted label. Then type a prompt (mock acks StreamSendMessage with a bare end_turn frame) and count the first replayed string: exactly 1 occurrence (0 = replay never rendered = vacuous; >1 = duplicate). Mirrors E2E cloud-resume-concurrent t1 + cloud-command-gates t6.
S06.limits: KAS's id-keyed dedup masks the original bug-#32 CLI-only path against a finite mock stream, so the dup-count check pins the layered dedup stack end-to-end; the original path needs a live-turn prod run.

S07.covers: Resume isolation (wrong-session replay would be a data leak between sessions)
S07.what: Resuming the EMPTY cloud sandbox while another session's history exists in the backend must replay nothing — no other session's conversation may leak into this session's scrollback.
S07.how: The mock keys canned history BY SESSION ID: banana has a transcript, the empty space serves only the session_loaded sentinel — with the history toggle ON, so the transcript exists and a wrong-session replay would be visible. Boot --resume-id <empty>, wait for the prompt, assert banana's transcript text is absent. Mirrors E2E cloud-resume-concurrent t2.

S08.covers: /clear viewport-residue bug (#3651's event-driven re-wipe); /clear = new-session semantics
S08.what: After /clear in a cloud session, none of the pre-clear conversation may remain readable. This regressed because cloud session/new keeps repainting the startup checklist for seconds AFTER the single scrollback wipe, so the wipe must win the race.
S08.how: Resume banana with history (seeds the viewport with a known transcript), frame it, type /clear, wait for the new prompt, then sleep 10s — past the re-wipe window's 8s max (CLOUD_CLEAR_REWIPE_DELAYS_MS=[1500,4000,8000]) — and assert the pre-clear text is gone. Before/after frames captured. Mirrors E2E cloud-command-gates t5.

S09.covers: Basic user stories 4 (list sessions) + 7 (multiple concurrent sessions); session switching
S09.what: /sessions lists ALL cloud sessions concurrently (the mock serves 4 spaces) with per-row environment tags, and picking a different session from the picker loads THAT session — replaying its own distinct transcript, not the current session's.
S09.how: Boot with MOCK_BFF_CONCURRENT=1 + MOCK_BFF_HISTORY=1. Open /sessions, assert both extra spaces render and the row-scoped 'cloud' tag (regex ties the tag to the row text, so titles can't fake it). Filter-type 'refactor' in the picker's incremental search (deterministic selection — no sort-order trust), press Enter, and assert the WORKING session's distinct one-turn transcript replays while banana's transcript is absent. Mirrors E2E cloud-resume-concurrent t3/t4.
S09.limits: Per-row LIVE status (working/waiting) is not asserted: KAS 0.26.x's listing carries no per-space execution status (every remote row reads idle). The mock's GetSessionStatus already serves the statuses for when KAS ships it.

S10.covers: Basic user story 6 (disconnect without killing; prompt before exiting)
S10.what: /disconnect detaches from the cloud session while the sandbox keeps working ('work continues while you're away' + a --resume-id reattach hint). /quit asks keep-running vs turn-off; choosing keep-running detaches the same way.
S10.how: Two boots. First: /disconnect, wait for the detach notice, assert the reattach hint names --resume-id. Second: /quit, wait for the keep-running prompt, select the first option (Enter), wait for the same detach notice. Frames at each state. Mirrors E2E cloud-sessions t5/t6.

S11.covers: Bug #23's shape (prompts duplicated in steer queue after ctrl+c/esc)
S11.what: Cancelling composed input with ctrl+c and then typing + sending a new message must produce exactly ONE sent message — no duplicate from a stale steer-queue entry.
S11.how: Type a draft, ctrl+c, type a unique marker, Enter, then count marker occurrences on screen: exactly 1 (0 would mean the send never rendered = vacuous; >1 = the duplication bug). Mirrors the smoke-script check; the full mid-TURN variant (cancel during a running turn) needs a live turn and is prod-smoke scope.
S11.limits: The mock never runs a real turn, so this exercises the input/keystroke path only — the queue-during-turn duplication path is prod scope.

S12.covers: Bug #34 (local file attached to a cloud session was a dead local path); fix #3652's send-time scan — text AND image variants
S12.what: When a prompt references a local file, the file's BYTES must ship in-band to the backend (the sandbox can never read the user's disk). Text files ship as resource blocks; images (the visible half of bug #34 — screenshots dragged into the prompt) ship as base64 image blocks with their MIME type. The proof is on the wire, not the UI.
S12.how: Two probes, each as the FIRST prompt of its own boot (the mock never ends a turn, so a second prompt in the same session queues as steer and never reaches the wire). Text: temp file whose CONTENT is a unique marker, 'read <path>', grep the mock BFF's decoded-request log for the marker. Image: real 1x1 PNG, 'describe <path>', grep the log for an image/png block. Both prove the send-time scan (utils/cloud-attach.ts) expanded the path into in-band content. Mirrors E2E cloud-file-attach.test.ts; the 23-test unit suite covers path forms (quoted/spaces/U+202F screenshot names), format table, size caps, and local parity.
S12.limits: The agent's REPLY about the file needs a live turn (mock acks without answering); the live round-trip ('agent read the blue PNG') was verified in the 0722 live-E2E pass and is prod-smoke scope here.

S13.covers: Opt-in semantics (dark-ship adjacent): cloud must never activate implicitly
S13.what: With the exact same environment (endpoint env var present, test mode on) but WITHOUT --cloud, the session boots plain local: no cloud checklist, no cloud surfaces.
S13.how: Boot with no args; wait for the local prompt; assert 'Cloud session created' never rendered. A scoped error check runs (tolerating only the sandboxed test HOME's known 'N MCP failure' row — a test-env artifact). Mirrors E2E cloud-sessions t7. The RELEASED-build darkness (rollout off entirely) is separately pinned by crates/chat-cli/tests/cloud_sessions_gating.rs at release profile.
S13.limits: This scenario proves opt-in under test mode, NOT the released rollout gate — that lives in the Rust release-profile suite.

S14.what: The headless `chat --list-sessions` (no TUI) shows cloud sessions merged with local ones, each tagged with the environment column ('| cloud |').
S14.how: Run the real binary headless against the mock BFF (KIRO_TEST_TUI_JS_PATH unset so no TUI boots), strip ANSI, assert the listing renders and cloud rows carry the tag. Output saved as a text artifact (no PTY frame). The full column/delete/prefix matrix is the Rust integration suite (cloud_sessions_gating.rs).

S15.covers: /autonomous on|off (#3653 CLI) — now end-to-end: KAS 0.27.8 relays session/set_mode for cloud sessions (forwardCoreVerb -> SendAcpMessage), so the previously-skipped scenario is live
S15.what: In a cloud session, /autonomous with no argument opens an on/off picker with the current state tagged [current] (on the OFF row for a fresh session); '/autonomous on' switches the session to the bundled autonomous agent mode, '/autonomous off' switches back to default, and repeating either says 'already on/off'. The CLI VERIFIES every switch by reading the mode back from the sandbox before printing success — so 'Autonomous mode on' is evidence of an applied switch, never a blind echo. With the 0.27.8 relay in place, the honest 'not supported on this session yet' fallback appearing would itself be a regression.
S15.how: Boot --cloud against the mock BFF, which plays the sandbox's core for forwarded verbs: SendAcpMessage applies session/set_mode to a per-session mode register and answers the session/set_config_option read-back with configOptions whose mode select reflects the register. Bare /autonomous: pin '[current]' AND that it sits on the off row (regex 'off +\[current\]'). '/autonomous on': wait for 'Autonomous mode on', assert the not-supported fallback is absent, and grep the BFF's decoded op log for the forwarded 'session/set_mode' — proof the switch crossed the wire rather than being locally faked. Then 'already on' idempotence, then '/autonomous off' -> 'Autonomous mode off'. Ends with the global no-error check. Frames at picker/on/off. Mirrors E2E cloud-autonomous.test.ts.
S15.limits: The mock applies the mode durably; whether the PRODUCTION sandbox core does (vs reverting on the next config push — the revert-detector path in kas.ts) needs a prod-scope run. An autonomous TURN (the agent acting autonomously) is out of scope: the mock never runs turns.

S16.covers: 07/31 outage signature (#3797): BFF stops routing the bearer service; #3720's user-facing guidance
S16.what: When the BFF's fronting layer answers operations itself instead of routing them to the service (the 07/31 production outage: every --cloud create/list failed as 'createSession: UnknownError'), the user must get the classified version-skew guidance — 'out of sync… Update kiro' — with the boot checklist marking the failure, not a bare UnknownError and not a silent local fallback that looks like success.
S16.how: Boot --cloud against the mock BFF in MOCK_BFF_UNROUTED=1 mode, which answers EVERY op with the router's bodyless no-code error so the real KAS Smithy client flattens it to '<op>: UnknownError' — the exact string observed live. Wait for 'Cloud session failed' on the checklist, then the 'out of sync' guidance, assert 'Update kiro' names the recovery action, and assert 'Cloud session created' never rendered. This is the one scenario whose SUBJECT is an error screen, so it asserts the guidance instead of running the no-error invariant. Mirrors E2E cloud-version-skew.test.ts; the classifier's string table is unit-pinned in cloud-error-classify.test.ts.
S16.limits: Pins the boot-time (session/new) path. Mid-session skew — a turn or listing failing after a successful boot — shares the classifier but its surfacing paths (turn error rows) are covered by the ordering test from #3821 and prod-smoke scope.

S17.covers: /spec cloud gate with PRE-FED local specs — the scope-mismatch class of #3690 (local config presented as sandbox state) applied to .kiro/specs
S17.what: Every /spec form reads the LOCAL .kiro/specs tree under the CLI's cwd, which is not the sandbox clone a cloud session runs on. In a cloud session each form (/spec, /spec run <name>, …) must refuse with '/spec is not available for a cloud session yet.' and the seeded local spec must never render — no picker row, no document list, no armed follow-on state. The same seeded workspace WITHOUT --cloud must drive the real flows (picker lists the feature), proving the gate is cloud-scoped rather than /spec being broken.
S17.how: Seed a temp workspace with .kiro/specs/checkout-flow/{requirements,tasks}.md and launch knight-rider with --workspace pointing at it. Cloud pass: /spec then /spec run checkout-flow, each waiting for the gate message; leak probe greps the screen for 'checkout-flow' on rows that are not the typed command echo; ends with the global no-error check. Local control pass: relaunch without --cloud in the same workspace, /spec must list checkout-flow with no gate message. Frames at spec-gate/spec-run-gate/spec-local-control. Mirrors E2E cloud-spec.test.ts (which also pins new/view/analyze_requirements forms and that nothing crosses the BFF wire).
S17.limits: Pins the gate, not spec functionality in cloud — when /spec becomes sandbox-aware (reads the sandbox clone's .kiro/specs over the relay), this scenario flips from asserting refusal to asserting the sandbox-side flows; the mock BFF's SendAcpMessage responder is ready to model the mode relay when that lands.

S18.covers: Subagent view in cloud sessions (bug #12 flattened-view seam; #3657 invoke_sub_agent rendering port)
S18.what: The sandbox KAS delegates via invoke_sub_agent, and on replay the fold strips _meta, leaving the meta-stripped 'Sub-agent: <role>' title shape. The CLI's cloud-only InvokeSubagentPipelineAdapter must claim that card and render the delegation identifiably (role visible) with its completed status honored — a bare flat tool row is the flattened view bug #12 reported, and a 'Cancelled' resurface is bug #2's shape applied to the subagent card. Surrounding turns must replay intact around the delegation.
S18.how: Resume the banana space against the mock BFF with MOCK_BFF_HISTORY=1 MOCK_BFF_SUBAGENT=1, which appends a canned turn containing a completed invoke_sub_agent delegation (payload toolName 'Sub-agent: api-auditor', args carrying name/explanation/prompt — the exact shape KAS's replay fold emits). Wait for the audit turn, assert 'api-auditor' renders, assert no Cancelled/interrupted, assert the prior turn also replayed (its ORDER relative to the subagent turn is pinned by the E2E mirror, not here), run the no-error check. Frame at subagent-replay. Mirrors E2E cloud-subagent-view.test.ts; the adapter's claim/labeling logic is unit-pinned in invoke-subagent-pipeline.test.ts.
S18.limits: Replay path only. A LIVE delegation (streaming stage updates, crew monitor interaction, approval routing through stages) needs an agent actually running turns — prod-smoke scope; the mock never runs a model. The crew/workflow monitor over cloud sessions is covered separately (workflow monitor suites) and is out of this scenario's scope.
